method_limits: a binding is followed only when the template is the whole right-hand side or sits inside it; a template embedded in a dict/list literal that is then subscripted is bound to the container, not to the leaf, and lands in the unread state.

exactly one rebinding hop is followed. A second hop is not, so the read count is a lower bound and the unread count is an upper bound; the size of that gap is not published here (a two-hop pass belongs to whoever prices the residue).

an opener is counted by call name (E426's vocabulary: open/read_*/json.load). A helper that takes the name and opens inside itself is invisible, so 'the opener reads it' means 'the name reaches a call that this census calls an opener'.
name matching is by identifier, not by scope resolution: a same-named local shadowing the target inside the same function would count as a read.
the corpus is the same python corpus E426 walks; it excludes Money02/legacy and it excludes results/, so a template built only by a notebook or a shell script is out of population, not zero.
